image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of the dorsal side of a large whale swimming in green water. The skin is dark grey with significant mottling and white patches (barnacles/callosities). A distinct longitudinal ridge runs along the back. A yellow object (likely part of a boat or kayak) is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a close-up of the mid-body/back; the head and blowholes are outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey coloration with white scarring and barnacle patches typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no dorsal fin. Instead, a series of low humps (knuckles) and a prominent ridge are visible along the spine, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The curvature and width of the body visible in the frame suggest a massive, robust spindle shape consistent with a large whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed visually; the texture and coloration are accurate to the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the whale is not visible; baleen plates are internal/oral structures not seen in this dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the ventral/lateral side and are not visible in this top-down dorsal shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
